description: Stackable one-piece moulded plastic armchair with a fan-patterned back, curved arms and tapered legs

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Stackable one-piece moulded plastic garden armchair, curved backrest with a broad fan pattern, integral curved arms flowing into the front legs, dished seat, four tapered ribbed legs Materials: sun-faded white polypropylene going chalky and yellow, grime in the mouldings, mould seams, black scuffs on the arms and leg feet.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.90. 1736/2000 triangles, 1/2 draw calls, 1/2 materials, 1/4 unique geometries, one canvas. Turntable with --allow-holes: the enclosed background is the five wedge slots, real openings. v4: with the flanks under the arms open, the 90/270 frames carry one real enclosed opening each (hole-check thickest 62.8 px, the space between arm, seat, leg and back), so --allow-holes is now justified by that measured opening rather than by the slot rims alone; the 90/270 silhouette ratios read 0.733 against 0.90 with the webs, because the flank area is gone.

featureReviews.evidence: Built 0.590 x 0.806 x 0.588 m against the declaration of 0.59 x 0.80 x 0.57. v2 lays every z station out from the proxy's BACK PLANE: back top 0-0.06 m from it, rear feet 0.06-0.12 m (v1 stood them 0.15 m further forward and the side view showed the back top cantilevered past them), arms 0.023-0.52 m (v3 sweeps: rib end to nose), seat 0.135-0.55 m, front feet at 0.515 m. Back read as two slopes off the proxy's z profile (30 degrees to 0.56, 14 above); top band 0.44-0.50 wide against the proxy's 0.39-0.46 where v1 fanned to 0.58.
featureReviews.notes: bands.mjs rotates the reference on this near-square plan (proxy w/h 0.739 vs d/h 0.712 against a built 0.59 x 0.588), so the stations were read off the occupancy map's z ranges directly.

featureReviews.evidence: The plate's back is a SOLID shell with five narrow wedge slots under a rounded top rail: six ribs on centres fanning 0.068 -> 0.074 (slots 16 -> 22 mm), the outer two slots filled over their lower half as the plate shows them short, a three-piece rail with its ends dropped 6 degrees, over a 0.43 wide band. (v3, owner review) each arm is ONE moulded elliptical sweep 0.085 x 0.034 that rises in an eased curve out of the outer rib, runs level at 0.616 and plunges into the top of the front leg (v4, owner review: the 20 mm side webs and the front fin blocks are gone, the flank under each arm is open and the front leg is one tapered fin from the foot to 0.53) -- connected to the back and the leg at both ends, where v2's flat box stopped 37 mm short of the ribs.
featureReviews.notes: v1 shipped five free slats with 60 mm gaps and open windows under the arms, which read as a wooden garden chair; v2's arms were flat boxes hanging short of the back. The rail's arc is three straight pieces.

featureReviews.evidence: Seat pan r 0.228 inside a 0.47 x 0.41 apron, 28 radial slot marks and 8 dots in mid-grey at luma 132, four fin legs stopping at the seat top (v5), tapering from 0.064 x 0.086 (front) and 0.060 x 0.044 (rear) at 0.45 to 0.040 x 0.060 with dark caps lifted on chroma, the rear pair continued by a 0.06 x 0.04 edge rib leaning 17 degrees up the side of the back into the arm root; rear feet at z -0.195 and front at +0.23 for the proxy's 0.485 m spread (v1 0.37).

name: Monobloc Plastic Armchair
nameTh: เก้าอี้พลาสติกมีท้าวแขน
notes: The single most repeated seat in Thailand and distinct from the existing Monobloc Plastic Stool, which is a backless dished disc -- this one has a back and arms and a completely different silhouette. Keep the back pattern as a few broad closed openings rather than a fine grille; a dense fretwork back is the classic way this chair blows a poly budget. Declared 0.55 x 0.80 x 0.55 m, inside the street-furniture prior of 0.3-1.8 m. PLAN CORRECTED FROM THE PROXY BEFORE BUILDING (2026-08-31): declared 0.55 x 0.80 x 0.55 (w/h = d/h 0.6875); the Meshy proxy measures w/h 0.739 and d/h 0.712, inside tolerance but 7% wider, so with height kept (a monobloc armchair is 0.78-0.82 m) the plan is 0.80 x 0.739 = 0.59 by 0.80 x 0.712 = 0.57. Seat top 0.56 H, arms 0.72-0.80 H, back leaning ~25 degrees, legs as tapered fins under the arm fronts and the seat back corners.
